subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a cron-specific tool policy such as `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep only per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but choosing the permanent scheduled-run tool boundary adds public config and security-sensitive precedence semantics that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling two different runtime concepts.

options.title: Keep current safeguards only
options.body: Leave cron control to per-job `toolsAllow` and duplicate-delivery safeguards, which keeps config smaller but does not solve the requested operator deny boundary.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and recent scoped conversation/cron history make `steipete` the strongest available decision owner signal.
